name: Anti-intellectualism
summary: Anti-intellectualism is a resentment and suspicion of the life of the mind and of those held to represent it, with a disposition to minimize the value of that life. In the political record it appears as distrust of experts and educated elites, a preference for common sense, practical experience and amateurs over training, and a stress on feeling over learning in religion.
scope: The attitude complex as Hofstadter defines it in Anti-intellectualism in American Life (1963) and the Gale encyclopedia entry summarizing it: a cluster of attitudes rather than a programme, documented mainly in American religion, politics and education. Primary text: William Jennings Bryan's Orthodox Christianity versus Modernism (1923), which Hofstadter cites for the anti-expert, majority-over-scientists case. It names no thinkers, parties or constitutional programme, so most statements about policy, the economy, foreign affairs and rights are unanswered.
